evidence_items.claim: NatWest is a FINOS Gold member, joined to engage with open source financial services projects starting with FDC3
evidence_items.excerpt: Our decision to join FINOS demonstrates our commitment to the natural open source contributor progression of 'learn, consume, participate, contribute, and lead' - Jennifer Scott, Head of Digital Technology NatWest Markets

evidence_items.claim: NatWest participated in FCA/BOE Digital Regulatory Reporting pilot Phases 1 and 2 (2018-2019) as one of 7 banks
evidence_items.excerpt: In 2018 and 2019, the 2 UK regulators collaborated with 7 banks to complete 2 pilots. The banks were Barclays, Credit Suisse, HSBC, Lloyds, Nationwide, NatWest and Santander.

evidence_items.claim: NatWest is a founding contributor to FINOS Fluxnova, an open source orchestration platform launched October 2025
evidence_items.excerpt: Fluxnova shows what's possible through open collaboration - creating shared solutions that make innovation faster and more accessible across the industry - James McLeod, Open Source Program Lead at NatWest Group

evidence_items.claim: NatWest is actively engaging with FINOS Git Proxy project for secure open source repository access
evidence_items.excerpt: NatWest's engineering approach is driving modern tooling, rapid customer value and a collaborative culture - like most organisations we are built on and proud to contribute to Open Source projects.

evidence_items.claim: NatWest presented at OSFF London 2024 on 'Pioneering a Successful Open Source First Culture at NatWest Group' and was a conference sponsor
evidence_items.excerpt: NatWest Group hosted a FINOS member-only roundtable on Open Source Supply Chain Security for the DevOps Automation SIG.

evidence_items.claim: NatWest offers EMIR Trade Reporting Service for OTC derivatives to clients under both EU and UK EMIR regulations
evidence_items.excerpt: NatWest Markets Plc reports the in-scope OTC derivatives when facing UK NFC- entities. NWM NV reports the in-scope OTC derivatives when facing EU/EEA NFC- entities.

evidence_items.claim: NatWest Markets trading assets increased 43% to €6.7 billion in 2024, indicating active derivatives business
evidence_items.excerpt: Trading assets increased by €1,995 million, or 43%, to €6,688 million in 2024.

evidence_items.claim: NatWest Markets Quantitative Analytics teams develop models and tools for derivatives and algorithmic trading using Python and C++
evidence_items.excerpt: Design and implement systems in a Python-based infrastructure that trades billions of dollars a day, creating models used for derivative pricing.

No evidence of CDM production deployment. EMIR reporting uses traditional approach.
